title: Marking a PR ready is not instant: priority decides, because a ready PR can hog CI from lanes that need it first
ruling: Owner 01:52 CST Nov 14 (typed in the consultant chat, relayed 01:53 CST): marking a PR ready instantly needs thought, because by priority it can hog CI from lanes that need it first. What the owner said: do not mark instantly; think about priority. The consultant's reading, NOT the owner's words: a batch runner marks handed-in PRs ready in priority order and only while CI has free slots (macOS is the scarce one); the three runners share one priority order across repos because one account's runner pool serves them all. Whether "only while CI has free slots" and the shared order are the owner's intent is unconfirmed. Home as the consultant gives it: the session-tiers batch-runner bullet and the rolling-train lane (step batch-runner-rolling-train). Neighbour: step priority-vs-merge-order and ruling own-817-a-priority-rows (the owner's priority rows). It qualifies, and does not undo, the standing grant "Lane draft PR" (a lane never marks ready; only the batch runner does): the runner marks ready, by priority, not at once. It also corrects triage's 01:50 CST line "runners mark each handed-in PR ready at once", which the owner's word overrides. SECOND OWNER WORD, 01:53 CST Nov 14 (consultant 01:54 CST, verbatim as relayed): "the number of slots cant be a static number btw it can change yk". So the slot count is not a fixed number; the consultant reads: the runner reads live queue state (queued jobs per leg) before each ready mark. The coordinator's reading (01:53 CST, relayed, also not the owner's words): ready in wave-plan priority order (CI-speed first), slot count measured from queued-job times, macOS the scarce slot tonight, one priority order across the three runners and every repo because one account's runner pool serves them all; the coordinator withdrew its 01:47 "mark ready at once" relay to the runners. Reading 2 (coordinator 01:54 CST, relayed, the consultant's; a reading, not the owner's words): no fixed slot count; before each ready mark the runner reads live free capacity once, inside its existing wake (any queued macOS job means macOS is full; queued Linux or Windows jobs mean that leg is full) and marks the next PR by priority only if the leg its run needs has no queue. A read inside the existing wake adds no timer or process (rule outcomes-mechanize-rules).
